AII-1000-31293: In November 2025, a hacker using the moniker ellie.191 conducted a supply chain attack against Suno and obtained source code revealing the company's data scraping practices. Reported impact Deezer stated it has always been on the side of artists and that training data for generative AI should be obtained with clear approval and fair compensation, adding that any infringement should be sanctioned. The company said it was assessing the situation and considering available options. A Suno spokesperson claimed the hack was quickly contained after discovery in November 2025, that the exposed code was outdated and no longer in use, and that no sensitive user information was compromised since the company does not retain full credit card numbers. Index analysis The hack provides evidence for ongoing copyright infringement lawsuits against Suno brought by record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music Entertainment and Warner Music Group, validating their allegations that Suno used artists' songs without consent or proper licensing. Governance controls Suno stated in public filings that its AI models have been trained on publicly available music files accessible on third-party websites on the open internet. The company concluded that under current privacy laws it did not need to notify individual users of the breach.
AII-1001-46341: A 15-second video purporting to show a tiger attacking and dragging a man near the Brahmapuri Forest Guest House in Chandrapur district went viral on social media on October 31, 2025. The video showed a tiger emerging through a gate and approaching a man seated in a chair. Forest officials noted that social media accounts of those sharing the video were being flagged for action, and the public was urged to report individuals spreading false wildlife-related information to forest or police authorities. Governance controls Deolapar Police registered a case against the Mumbai-based social media user responsible for the earlier AI-generated petting video. The Maharashtra Forest Department initiated action and issued an official statement clarifying that no tiger attack had occurred. Chief Conservator of Forests RM Ramanujam appealed to citizens not to fall prey to rumours and called for immediate reporting of false information distribution to nearest forest or police authorities.
AII-1001-44999: Food delivery shops in China are using AI-generated images and manipulated videos to misrepresent their storefronts. Reported impact Consumer Wang in Beijing's Chaoyang District found a rice restaurant with an AI-generated storefront image showing an outdoor location with prominent signage and crowds at the entrance and inside. Upon investigation, she discovered the shop was actually a basement-level vendor stall in a food court with no dedicated dining area, and across the platform three identically-named shops shared the same fake image with reported sales of over 400,000 units. According to a lawyer at Beijing De Heng Law Firm, vendors using false pictures and videos infringe on consumers' right to know and right of choice. Service providers who knowingly supply such materials for false or misleading commercial promotion may be liable. Index analysis Fake storefronts created with AI images and video compositing mislead consumers who tend to select delivery vendors they perceive as high-quality dine-in establishments. The low cost of generating AI images and modifying real photos has made creating 'virtual storefronts' a shortcut for some delivery vendors, with such services widely advertised on secondary market and short-video platforms. Governance controls The State Administration for Market Regulation drafted a regulation requiring third-party platforms to display a 'no dine-in' label on the platform's listing page and on the homepage of vendors that do not provide dine-in service.
AII-1001-44769: U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn, a Tennessee Republican, sent a letter to Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai accusing Google's AI model Gemma of generating "false and defamatory" content about her and other conservatives. AII-1001-44727: Two autonomous security robots equipped with 360-degree and thermal imaging cameras patrolled the Basel Autumn Fair overnight between 11 p.m. and 8 a.m. to monitor the fairground. AII-1001-44703: Caitlin Roper, a member of the Australian activist group Collective Shout, received AI-generated death threats and violent images showing her dead in various scenarios, including hanging from a noose and ablaze. AII-1001-44633: A mother in Florida sued Character Technologies in the previous year, alleging the company bore responsibility for her 14-year-old son's suicide, which the teen had preceded with intensive use of the company's chatbot. AII-1001-44201: The Metropolitan Police reported that between September 2024 and September 2025, 962 people were arrested following deployments of Live Facial Recognition (LFR) technology. AII-1003-06663: On 30 October 2025, Seo Kyung-duk, a professor at Sungshin Women's University, reported that Naver's AI Briefing service returned Dokdo as Japanese territory when users searched 'Japanese territory' or 'Japan territory' in Korean. Index analysis The AI Briefing service is designed to minimize confusion and error in public and policy information by basing answers on public documents from government agencies. However, the system generated misleading territorial claims by relying on foreign government sources without domestic verification or context. Governance controls Naver stated it took immediate action upon recognizing the issue and committed to enhanced service improvements to ensure AI Briefing generates results better suited to queries, with plans for continuous refinement. AII-1001-51749: On 30 October 2025, a JetBlue A320 en route from Cancun, Mexico to Newark, New Jersey experienced an uncontrolled descent without pilot commands, descending approximately 25,000 feet. The scale of the recall reflects the aircraft's dominance in global aviation. AII-1001-46311: A six-second AI-generated video posted to Instagram on October 30, 2025, showed a man giving liquor to a tiger and patting the animal on an empty village street. Reported impact Police stated the video sent a wrong message and could damage the image of Pench Tiger Reserve, potentially misleading tourists and affecting tourism to the reserve. The video also presented a misleading and dangerous view of how to behave around wild animals. Index analysis The incident demonstrates the rapid spread of AI-generated misinformation on social media platforms, particularly content falsely linked to wildlife reserves and named individuals, creating fabricated narratives that could undermine public trust in wildlife protection efforts and tourism. Governance controls Nagpur Rural Police issued a legal notice to the Instagram user and appealed to citizens to stop sharing fake content, warning of action against those who create content that defames wildlife reserves or spreads misinformation.
AII-1001-44621: Fake Airbnb and Booking.com rental scams surged across Europe in 2024–2025, with fraudsters using AI-generated profiles, fabricated reviews, and phishing sites mimicking legitimate platforms. Common tactics included off-platform payment requests, fake customer support, and AI-crafted host profiles. The scheme expanded from Paris, Rome, and Prague to Barcelona, Lisbon, and the Canary Islands. In response, Airbnb removed 59,000 fake listings, blocked thousands more, and deployed fraud detection AI and user education campaigns. Meanwhile, Airbnb uses automated anti-party technology to block bookings flagged as high-risk based on factors such as reservation length and last-minute booking requests. Last year the system deterred about 38,000 bookings in the United States and about 6,300 in Canada. Reported impact Victims of rental scams lost on average £1,937 each. Tourists arriving for vacations in Paris, Rome, and Prague found their booked addresses nonexistent or occupied, leaving them stranded. Airbnb's anti-party blocking system has flagged legitimate bookings as high-risk, preventing some guests from completing reservations over the Halloween weekend and other periods. Index analysis Travel-related phishing and fake listing scams rose '500–900% in 18 months' by 2024, according to Booking.com's safety chief, driven partly by AI-generated fakes. Australia's Scamwatch program reported a 600% surge in accommodation booking scams in 2023, with 363 reports mentioning Booking.com compared to 53 in 2022. Airbnb's automated anti-party technology uses machine learning to flag bookings as risky based on patterns such as short reservation windows and last-minute requests, which can catch legitimate holiday bookings. Governance controls Paris imposed €100,000 fines and night limits on short-term rentals; Rome worked with cyber-police; Prague implemented a registration system for vacation rental properties to curb fraudulent listings.
AII-1001-44529: The Sixth Panel of Brazil's Superior Court of Justice (STJ) upheld the validity of evidence obtained through automated scanning of peer-to-peer file-sharing networks using Child Rescue Coalition (CRC) software. The investigation targeted a dentist in Mato Grosso do Sul accused of storing child sexual abuse material, as part of Operation Predator conducted by the Civil Police. The court ruled that police do not require prior judicial authorization to scan public virtual environments where users share files or to request Internet service providers for subscriber information linked to specific IP addresses. Justice Rogerio Schietti Cruz, the rapporteur, found that monitoring in a virtually public environment where users voluntarily share files and expose their IP addresses does not constitute privacy invasion or unlawful wiretapping. Reported impact Based on software results, police obtained a search warrant, located electronic equipment, and found pornographic images involving children and adolescents. The dentist was identified and prosecuted following the scan. Index analysis The defendant's legal team argued that the evidence was unlawful due to lack of prior judicial authorization, but the court rejected this position. The court concluded that the tracking of shared files does not imply invasion of private space or interception of communications. Governance controls The STJ decision establishes that police may use automated scanning software in peer-to-peer networks without pre-approval from a judge, provided the scanning targets publicly accessible virtual environments where users voluntarily share files.
AII-1001-44519: The Bank of Korea analysed the impact of AI expansion on youth employment using national pension subscriber data, categorising industries by AI exposure levels. Since ChatGPT's release in November 2022, youth job losses concentrated in high-exposure sectors, totalling 211,000 positions lost between July 2022 and July 2025. In the same period, over 98.6% of lost youth jobs (208,000) occurred in high-exposure industries, while workers aged 50+ saw 209,000 new positions created, with 69.9% in high-exposure sectors. Computer programming, system integration and management (-11.2%), information services (-23.8%), publishing (-20.4%), and professional services (-8.8%) experienced the largest youth employment declines. Reported impact Youth workers perform routinised, standardised tasks that AI readily substitutes, while mid-career and senior workers handle context-dependent, interpersonal and organisational management roles that AI cannot easily replace. The Bank of Korea stated that early AI expansion showed youth employment contracting while mid-career employment expanded, a pattern termed 'senior-biased technological change'. In sectors where AI complements rather than replaces human work, such as healthcare, education and aviation, youth employment did not decline. Wage effects from AI adoption were not yet clearly observable. Index analysis Youth with intermediate to advanced education levels faced greater vulnerability to AI replacement, with work-hour reductions of 7.6% for master's degree holders and 5.0% for four-year university graduates, compared to 3.7% for doctorates and 0.8% for high school graduates. The Bank of Korea noted that whether the initial youth employment contraction will continue is uncertain, and that companies may face talent pipeline degradation from reduced youth hiring, creating incentives to develop AI-collaborative workforce strategies and job redesign.
AII-1001-44489: IIT Delhi researchers developed AndroCon, a system that uses fine-grained GPS data already accessible to Android apps with precise location permissions to infer sensitive contextual information without explicit user consent. The system interprets nine low-level GPS parameters including Doppler shift, signal power, and multipath interference to determine whether someone is sitting, standing, or lying down, their location type (metro, flight, park, crowded space), and whether a room is crowded or empty. The framework can also sketch indoor floor maps identifying rooms, staircases, and elevators with a margin of error under 4 metres using only GPS patterns and user trajectories. Reported impact The study exposes a critical security gap in Android permissions. Any Android app with precise location permissions could potentially infer sensitive contextual information about users without their explicit consent. Index analysis AndroCon achieved up to 99 per cent accuracy in detecting surroundings and over 87 per cent accuracy in recognising human activities across a year-long study spanning 40,000 square kilometres and multiple phone devices.
AII-1001-43997: Sewell Setzer III, a 14-year-old, died by suicide in February 2025 after months of intimate exchanges with a Character.AI chatbot modeled on the character Daenerys Targaryen from Game of Thrones, according to a lawsuit filed by his mother, Megan Garcia, against Character.AI. AII-1000-97429: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2025-12420) in ServiceNow's AI Platform infrastructure enables unauthenticated attackers to impersonate legitimate users and execute unauthorized operations. Governance controls ServiceNow strongly recommends that customers immediately apply security updates or upgrade to patched versions, with minimum versions specified as 5.1.18 or 5.2.19 for Assist AI Agents, and 3.15.2 or 4.0.4 for Virtual Agent API.
AII-1001-44409: A South Korean website called 玩X (Play X) enables users to upload photographs of female acquaintances—former girlfriends, spouses, and friends—and uses AI technology to generate realistic nude 3D figurines of those women. The platform operates with minimal access restrictions, requires only proof of age 18 or older, uses encrypted cryptocurrency for transactions to avoid financial tracking, and promises automatic deletion of IP addresses to shield members from identification. AII-1001-44339: On 29 October 2025, Honduras Attorney General Johel Zelaya publicly released audio recordings allegedly featuring voices of National Electoral Council (CNE) advisor Cossette López and National Party deputy Tomás Zambrano discussing a plan to alter results in the 30 November general elections. AII-1001-44267: On 28 October 2025, Orbán Balázs, campaign chief for Fidesz, published an AI-generated video depicting Magyar Péter, leader of the Tisza Párt, speaking about pensions in words he never said. AII-1001-44217: A Facebook account titled 'Man City Fan Lover' posted false stories about Manchester City footballer Phil Foden's children, claiming his four-year-old daughter True had been diagnosed with cancer and his six-year-old son Ronnie had died. AII-1001-44183: Researchers at the University of Basel tested state-of-the-art AI models including AlphaFold and RosettaFold to verify whether they understood the physics underlying protein-ligand interactions. The models had shown apparently high success rates in predicting how proteins interact with small molecules such as drugs. The researchers modified hundreds of sample proteins so that ligand binding sites had completely different charge distributions or were blocked entirely. In more than half of the cases, the AI models predicted the same complex structure as if binding were still possible, despite the modifications that should have prevented binding. The researchers tested a similar approach with modified ligands designed to be unable to dock to proteins, and the models again failed to recognize the problem. The researchers concluded that the models memorize patterns from training data rather than learning the underlying principles of physical chemistry. Reported impact The models struggled particularly with novel proteins that did not show similarity to training data, which are precisely the proteins of greatest interest for developing innovative drugs. According to the researchers, only around 100,000 protein structures together with their ligands were available for training the AI models, relatively few compared to other AI training datasets, yet the models achieved suspiciously high success rates. Index analysis The models' reliance on pattern matching rather than physical understanding means they may generate confident predictions for novel protein-ligand interactions that lack scientific validity, potentially misleading drug development efforts.
AII-1001-44027: From 29 October 2025, Foodstuffs South Island began a three-month trial of facial recognition technology at New World St Martins, PAK'nSAVE Papanui and PAK'nSAVE Moorhouse in Christchurch. Reported impact Foodstuffs said stores had been repeatedly targeted with serious, threatening behaviour even after individuals were trespassed, and the trial aims to help identify repeat offenders and prevent further harm. The Commissioner noted potential safety benefits despite the privacy concerns. Governance controls Foodstuffs engaged with the Office of the Privacy Commissioner and completed a Privacy Impact Assessment. AII-1001-44283: On October 28, 2025, during Nvidia's GTC keynote in Washington, DC, a deepfake video of CEO Jensen Huang was broadcast on YouTube on a channel called NVIDIA Live, promoted as a cryptocurrency investment opportunity. It is unknown whether any of the viewers sent money to the scammers. Index analysis The incident demonstrates the relative ease of creating convincing deepfakes with the abundance of video footage of Jensen Huang from multiple GTC conferences, which bad actors can use as training data for AI video generation systems.

AII-1001-41633: On Monday evening outside Kenwood High School in Baltimore County, Maryland, Omnilert's AI gun detection system sent an alert to school and police that a student had a weapon. AII-1001-43143: Following a daytime heist of jewels from the Louvre museum in Paris on October 19, multiple videos surfaced on social media claiming to show CCTV footage of the theft. AII-1001-41583: Italian researchers led by Vincenzo Guastafierro from the Clinical Institute and Università Humanitas in Rozzano near Milan conducted a study begun in 2023 analyzing ChatGPT responses to 200 clinical cases across different medical specializations. AII-1001-41567: A couple alleges in a lawsuit that ChatGPT told their son about specific methods for ending his life and offered to help write a suicide note. AII-1001-41357: Brazil's Tribunal Superior do Trabalho (TST) upheld a collective bargaining clause requiring compensation for doormen dismissed when condominiums replace in-person door stations with remote monitoring systems. AII-1001-41309: World Foundation and Tools for Humanity Corporation collected iris biometric images from thousands of people in Colombia in exchange for economic compensation. AII-1001-41133: A study led by Mass General Brigham researchers tested five advanced LLMs – three OpenAI ChatGPT models and two Meta Llama models – with illogical medical queries to assess their reasoning capabilities. The video included a small watermark stating 'AI GENERATED' in the bottom right corner and an additional 'Altered or synthetic content' label on YouTube. Reported impact The deepfake video raised alarms among observers who warned it crossed a new boundary in political campaigning and could unleash a flood of AI-generated deepfake attack ads, according to reporting. Professor Hany Farid of UC Berkeley, who studies manipulated media, stated that creating a deepfake was different from simply showing an image with an overlaid quote, and that the disclaimer was not particularly clear or obvious. Governance controls The NRSC included a small transparent watermark with the NRSC logo and the words 'AI GENERATED' in the bottom right-hand corner of the video. On YouTube, an additional 'Altered or synthetic content' label was applied to the video.
AII-1001-40841: Researchers at KASTEL Information Security and Reliability Institute at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology published research in ACM Data Science journal documenting a method for identifying individuals by analyzing Wi-Fi signal propagation patterns. The system uses passive monitoring of existing Wi-Fi signals in the environment to infer the identity of people present, without requiring any special hardware. The technique can identify individuals even if they are not actively using Wi-Fi or have their phones turned off. Reported impact The research describes a surveillance capability that enables person identification through walls, raising privacy concerns. Attackers could exploit ambient Wi-Fi signals to covertly determine who is present in a given location. Index analysis Prior research on Wi-Fi-based person detection includes earlier work on gait-based identification systems and techniques for observing human body contours through clothing.
AII-1001-41291: Three U.S. labor unions—the United Auto Workers (UAW), Communications Workers of America (CWA), and American Federation of Teachers (AFT)—filed a federal lawsuit in the Southern District of New York on October 16, 2025, against the Departments of State and Homeland Security. The complaint alleges that the government operates an artificial intelligence-powered surveillance program that monitors the social media accounts of visa holders and lawful permanent residents to identify and target those expressing disfavored viewpoints, including criticism of the United States, support for Palestine, or opposition to U.S. foreign policy. Reported impact The unions claim the surveillance program has had a chilling effect on lawful expression among noncitizens, coupled with a public campaign of intimidation warning that those posting anti-American or anti-Israel content risk deportation or visa revocation. According to a survey cited in the complaint, 80% of UAW members with visas who were aware of the program reported modifying their social media activity, and 40% of similarly situated CWA members reported the same. Index analysis The lawsuit raises constitutional questions about whether noncitizens living lawfully in the United States enjoy the same First Amendment protections as citizens, and whether immigration enforcement can be used to silence dissenting viewpoints. The Electronic Frontier Foundation argued that the program violates the First Amendment and the Administrative Procedure Act, noting that AI tools allow the government to analyze social media at a scale previously impossible through human review alone. Governance controls The plaintiffs have requested that a New York judge issue an order to stop the program. The unions argue that the surveillance program has undermined their ability to associate with their members and potential members.
AII-1001-41091: Around 11:40 p.m., a teenage boy in Malaysia received a message on Telegram from an unknown sender with no phone number. The message contained a personal photo of the boy and an AI-generated explicit video, with a demand for RM5,800 and threats to release the fabricated footage if he did not comply. The boy did not panic and sought advice from a trusted school contact who had experience helping another student who had faced a similar attack. His mother reported the incident to police the following morning. Reported impact Police officers told the family that this scheme is becoming increasingly common, with scammers using AI deepfake tools to create fake explicit content and threatening victims with exposure unless they pay. The officers warned that people of any age can be targeted. Governance controls Police advised that people experiencing similar harassment should document everything, not pay the extortionists, and report incidents to police and the platform immediately.
AII-1001-41079: On 4 June 2025, Judge Carlos Rogelio Richeri issued a sentence condemning Raúl Amelio Payalef to two years and six months of effective prison for theft. The ruling contained a phrase from an AI assistant: "Aquí tienes el punto IV reeditado, sin citas y listo para copiar y pegar" (Here you have section IV rewritten, without citations and ready to copy and paste), indicating that ChatGPT had been used to draft the decision. On 16 October 2025, the Cámara Penal de Esquel annulled the sentence on its own initiative, finding that the accidental inclusion of the AI assistant's prompt revealed the judge had used an artificial intelligence system to write the ruling without proper human supervision or control. Reported impact The annulment means the conviction is void and a new trial must be held before a different judge. The court found that the phrase exposed a fundamental breach of the principle of natural judge, which requires decisions to be made by a competent, independent and responsible human authority, not by an automated system. Index analysis The court stated that the "evidence of copy and paste" created too wide a gap to determine how much of the ruling was attributable to the AI system and how much to the judge. Without a record of what was asked of the program, what was obtained, and how it was integrated into the reasoning, the decision lacked verifiable grounds and could not be reviewed for soundness. Governance controls The court found that the judge failed to exercise proper human supervision and control when using the AI tool. The sentence was signed with a citation from the AI assistant but did not record the use of AI, what was asked of the program, or how the responses were incorporated into the judicial analysis. The Cámara Penal ordered the case forwarded to the Superior Tribunal de Justicia de Chubut for investigation of the judge's conduct.
AII-1001-41007: Seemingly harmless images of children shared online are being transformed using artificial intelligence into images depicting lightly clothed or naked children. These AI-manipulated materials are then distributed, sexualized, or placed in sexual contexts by child predators in the darknet. Reported impact The Bundeskriminalamt (BKA) received more than 200,000 reports of child sexual abuse material in the previous year, including such AI-altered images. The German federal government stated that such material is in circulation and that the volume of such material is generally increasing. Index analysis The BKA recommends that child images not be shared on the internet. The concern is that seemingly innocuous photos shared on social media by parents can be weaponized through AI technology and exploited by criminals. Governance controls The BKA, as the central police authority, is responsible for combating sexual abuse of children and issued guidance advising against sharing child images online. The German federal government acknowledged the problem and stated measures are in place to make it difficult for pedophiles while making it harder for offenders.
AII-1001-40967: AI music generation tools like Suno can create songs from text prompts that mimic the voices of celebrity artists, often without their knowledge or consent. YouTube videos presenting these AI-generated tributes falsely attributed them to artists including Adele, Ed Sheeran, and Justin Bieber, with fabricated thumbnails showing the artists in tears. One widely circulated example was an emotional tribute to slain US activist Charlie Kirk, presented with a comment saying 'Thank you, Adele, it's such a beautiful song,' though the music was AI-generated and bore little resemblance to Adele's voice. The videos collectively attracted millions of views and thousands of comments from viewers who believed the content was authentic and thanked the artists for songs they never created. Reported impact Unwitting users consumed content infused with AI-enabled disinformation and engaged with it as if it were authentic. In many cases, the AI voices sounded little like the original artists, yet scrollers still believed the fake content. The trend raised copyright issues and highlighted erosion of shared reality as consumers became passive recipients of misleading content created by what observers described as 'grifters aiming to make money.' Index analysis AI music generation tools have become widely accessible and can quickly produce realistic-sounding tributes from simple text prompts. YouTube's policy requires creators to disclose synthetic content, but disclosures are often buried in video descriptions where they are easily overlooked unless users click to expand the text.
AII-1001-40961: A 17-year-old girl from New Jersey filed a lawsuit against ClothOff developer AI/Robotics Venture Strategy 3 and Telegram. The plaintiff alleges that a high school classmate used ClothOff to generate deepfake nude images based on a clothed photo she posted to Instagram when she was 14 years old. According to the complaint, the classmate accessed ClothOff through Telegram's automated bot system. The plaintiff also alleges that several male classmates shared multiple deepfake nude images of female students in a group chat. Reported impact The plaintiff states she lives in 'endless fear' that the deepfake images will spread online. She expresses concern that her photos and those of other girls may have been used to train ClothOff's AI model. Index analysis The plaintiff's lawyers at Yale Law School identified that ClothOff is registered in the British Virgin Islands but is operated by people residing in Belarus. They expect that if operators do not appear in court or respond to the lawsuit, the court may block the software's use in the United States. Telegram stated that non-consensual sexual imagery and tools to create it are explicitly prohibited in its terms of service and are deleted when found. The company said it regularly removes bots designed to generate non-consensual sexual imagery, including those using ClothOff. Governance controls The San Francisco District Attorney filed lawsuits against 16 major deepfake-nude sites in the previous year, including ClothOff, resulting in approximately 10 closures. The District Attorney stated litigation against ClothOff continues.
AII-1001-40959: Reddit Answers, a conversational AI chatbot, recommended heroin and kratom for chronic pain management in health-related subreddits. A healthcare worker reported that the chatbot suggested a post stating 'Heroin, ironically, has saved my life in those instances' and recommended kratom, a tree extract illegal in multiple states. The chatbot appeared under posts in health and wellness subreddits where moderators could not report or block it. According to the FDA, kratom poses risks including liver toxicity, seizures, and substance use disorder. Reported impact A healthcare worker expressed concern that AI-generated content appearing under health posts could mislead users with limited medical literacy who rely on such recommendations for decision-making. Reddit users amplified dangerous anecdotes through the chatbot's suggestions, which trained on user-generated content from the platform. Index analysis Reddit Answers generates responses from user-generated content on the platform without medical verification. The chatbot recommended both legal and illegal substances as treatments, some encouraging users to discontinue prescribed medications. Governance controls After the issue was reported, Reddit reduced the feature's visibility under sensitive discussions and removed it from appearing in health-related subreddits.
AII-1001-40941: Auterion, a US software company, and an unnamed Ukrainian partner company developed the Artemis ALM-20, a long-range kamikaze drone with a range of 1600 km and a 45 kg warhead. The drone uses AI-powered visual guidance and the Skynode N onboard navigation computer to guide itself and strike targets, with the ability to operate without GPS or satellite navigation. The system has completed testing including ground launch, GPS and non-GPS navigation, long-distance transit, and ground impact. According to reports, it has already been used in strikes against Russia. Reported impact The drone reportedly provides Ukraine with a long-range autonomous strike capability that can function independently of satellite navigation systems. Index analysis The Artemis ALM-20 uses AI-guided visual targeting on an autonomous platform designed to strike targets without human intervention during the final phase of flight. The system integrates autonomous navigation and targeting into a single platform, raising questions about compliance with international humanitarian law regarding autonomous weapon systems. Governance controls Auterion stated that production will scale with the U.S. Department of Defense and other partners, with manufacturing lines being established in Ukraine, the United States, and Germany.
AII-1001-40917: Consob, Italy's financial regulator, blocked 17 websites that used deepfake videos of Italian politicians including Meloni, Salvini, Schlein and Calenda to promote unauthorized cryptocurrency and financial services. The sites featured manipulated video endorsements to fraudulently promote crypto assets and unlicensed investment products. Reported impact The deepfake advertisements were designed to deceive consumers into engaging with unauthorized crypto and financial services. Index analysis The use of synthetic media impersonating well-known political figures created the appearance of legitimate endorsement, bypassing consumer skepticism by exploiting the recognition and authority of the cloned individuals. Governance controls Consob identified and suspended the fraudulent sites, taking enforcement action against the unauthorized financial service providers.
AII-1001-40913: A 31-year-old company employee from Akita was arrested by the Metropolitan Police Department on suspicion of creating and distributing sexually obscene images of more than 260 female entertainers using generative AI software. The suspect used free AI image generation software to train a model on real actresses' images, then generated thousands of images using specific text prompts, and published them online. The suspect earned approximately 1.2 million yen by selling access to the images. According to investigators, he had no formal training in ICT or AI and learned how to use the technology from articles and videos online. He stated he began the activity as a side business after seeing similar images being monetized online, and continued because viewer reactions and popularity generated significant revenue. Reported impact More than 260 female entertainers were targeted by the synthetic sexual images created and distributed online without consent. The ease and low cost of the technology has led to expanding harm from similar incidents.
AII-1001-40853: Immigration barrister Chowdhury Rahman used ChatGPT-like software to prepare his legal research for a tribunal hearing in an asylum appeal case involving two Honduran sisters. Upper tribunal judge Mark Blundell found that 12 authorities were cited in Rahman's grounds of appeal, but some of those authorities did not exist and others did not support the propositions of law for which they were cited. Blundell stated: 'The most obvious explanation is … that the grounds of appeal were drafted in whole or in part by generative artificial intelligence such as ChatGPT.' The judge noted that one of the cases cited had 'recently been wrongly deployed by ChatGPT in support of similar arguments.' Reported impact Judge Blundell found that Rahman 'failed thereafter to undertake any proper checks on the accuracy' of the AI-generated content and had 'wasted' the tribunal's time. Blundell stated that 'not one decision supported the proposition of law set out in the grounds' and rejected Rahman's appeal, finding nothing in his submissions established an error of law. Index analysis The AI system generated multiple fictitious legal cases and citations that did not exist, demonstrating a hallucination failure mode that the barrister did not catch before submitting to the court. Rahman apparently tried to hide his use of AI and misled the court about the source of his legal research by claiming he had used 'various websites.' Governance controls Judge Blundell said he was considering reporting Rahman to the Bar Standards Board for disciplinary action.
AII-1001-40791: A manipulated video circulated online falsely portraying actor Manoj Bajpayee as endorsing a political party ahead of Bihar elections. The video was created by editing an advertisement Bajpayee had previously made for Prime Video India. Reported impact The deepfake video spread across social media platforms, potentially misleading voters about the actor's political affiliations during election campaigns. Index analysis The incident reflects a broader rise in misuse of celebrity videos and deepfake content during election periods. Governance controls Bajpayee publicly condemned the video on X (formerly Twitter), clarifying that he has no association with any political party and urging people to stop sharing the edited content.
AII-1001-40769: ESET identified a campaign called 'Grokking' in which attackers used prompt injection to manipulate Grok into spreading malicious links. Attackers posted videos with clickbait content on X and embedded fraudulent phishing or malware links in the video metadata where the source information is displayed. Reported impact The attackers asked Grok to identify the origin of the videos, and when the chatbot analyzed the posts, it detected and automatically repeated the fraudulent links in its responses, spreading them to millions of X users at scale. This technique allowed malicious actors to circumvent X's advertising restrictions designed to prevent malicious ads. Index analysis The attack relies on prompt injection, a technique where hidden instructions are embedded in content analyzed by AI systems to cause them to perform actions they normally have restrictions against. The fraudulent links direct victims to phishing pages designed to steal personal or banking data, or to malware downloads intended to compromise devices.
AII-1001-40731: Data annotators in Kenya and Colombia perform low-paid work labeling images and text to train generative AI systems. Kenyan worker Ivantous Kanyugi, 30, has classified and labeled images since 2018 for companies including Scale AI subsidiary Remotasks, earning only a few dollars or approximately $0.01 per task that may take hours. Venezuelan worker Oscarinа Fuentes, 35, working for five data annotation platforms in Colombia, earns between 5 and 25 cents per task. Workers report spending extended hours viewing graphic content from crime scenes without psychological support, experiencing visual problems, physical pain, and mental health issues from working up to 20 hours daily. Reported impact Data annotators experience visual problems, physical pain, and psychological distress from their work without adequate support. Workers describe their labor as invisible despite contributing to AI technology advancement. The data annotation market was valued at $3.77 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach $17.1 billion by 2030, yet the workers who train these systems remain underpaid and unprotected. Index analysis Generative AI systems require human verification of training data and evaluation of AI-generated outputs. Most data annotators are aged 18–30 from low-income countries, though the work is growing in the United States and Europe where wages are significantly higher. Technology companies including Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI outsource data annotation work to intermediary companies like Scale AI. Scale AI operates platforms including Outlier, which advertises specialist positions at $30–50 per hour, while its Remotasks subsidiary in Kenya pays approximately $0.01 per task. Governance controls Kenya lacks legal regulations for the data annotation sector. The Data Labelers Association in Nairobi, with approximately 800 members, plans to announce a code of conduct for data annotation platforms to improve working conditions. International labor organizations and civil society groups call for accountability from technology companies and fair employment contracts that include rest periods and psychological support. EU legislation reportedly does not address these workers.
AII-1001-40647: OpenAI announced on October 16 that it halted the use of Martin Luther King Jr.'s likeness in its video generation AI service Sora after disrespectful videos depicting the civil rights leader circulated online. Bernice King, daughter of Martin Luther King Jr., requested that OpenAI stop the practice. Videos also circulated of Malcolm X depicted making vulgar jokes and fighting with King. Reported impact Malcolm X's family stated that the disrespectful use of their father's likeness was "insulting and heartbreaking," saying the ideals of "truth" that he devoted his life to were "being exploited in a thoughtless and careless manner." Index analysis OpenAI initially claimed that videos of real people required consent and said it had included features to prevent celebrity impersonation, but excluded historical figures from these restrictions, arguing that depictions of historical figures have strong public interest and are protected by freedom of expression. Governance controls OpenAI halted the generation of videos depicting Martin Luther King Jr. in response to the complaints and offensive content.
AII-1001-40539: Digitally altered explicit images using the faces of female students from a Sydney high school were circulated online. A male student who was sent the images reported it to his school, after which families attended Eastwood Police Station. Reported impact The eSafety Commissioner stated that deepfake image-based abuse reports have doubled across Australia over the past 18 months, with at least one incident emerging from Australian schools each week. The NSW Department of Education said deepfakes present significant new risks to student wellbeing and privacy. Index analysis Officers from Ryde Police Area Command commenced an investigation. The eSafety Commissioner confirmed investigators were in talks with NSW Police and the NSW Department of Education over the circulation of the digitally altered explicit images. Governance controls The NSW Department of Education said the school was working closely with police and would take strong disciplinary action if any student was found to have engaged in the behaviour. Legislation passed by NSW Parliament last month made the production of sexually explicit deepfakes of a real, identifiable person without consent punishable by up to three years' jail.
AII-1001-46469: An online midterm exam held on 15 October in a class titled 'Natural Language Processing (NLP) and ChatGPT' with approximately 600 students at Yonsei University's Sinchon campus saw widespread cheating. Students bypassed proctoring measures by adjusting camera angles to create blind spots, overlaying multiple programs on screen, and capturing exam questions. Many students used ChatGPT and other AI systems during the exam. In an informal poll on the student community platform Everytime with 387 responses, 211 students reported cheating and 176 reported solving the exam honestly. The professor announced that admitted cheaters would receive zero points on the midterm, while students who deny cheating face expulsion. Reported impact By November, over 40 students had admitted to cheating. The university stated that 10 additional students suspected of cheating had not confessed. The midterm exam scores of all admitted cheaters were set to zero. Index analysis The incident reflects inadequate proctoring in remote exams and insufficient institutional governance on AI use in academic settings. According to research cited in reports, 71.1% of 131 surveyed universities nationwide lacked generative AI guidelines, and 91.7% of surveyed students had used AI in coursework or research. Governance controls The course required students to submit video footage showing their computer screen, hands, and face throughout the exam. However, these measures proved insufficient to prevent cheating.
AII-1001-43949: On the morning of 15 October, NTB published a news article about Telenor's annual security report. Shortly after, the entire article was withdrawn and replaced with different text. The original article contained five direct quotes that NTB stated were taken from Telenor's report, but none of these quotations could be found in the actual report. The article also named Håkon Berg as Telenor's security director and attributed a quote to him, but no such person has held this position at Telenor. The report's foreword was actually signed by CEO Birgitte Engebretsen. NTB's news editor Christina Dorthellinger Nygaard confirmed that the erroneous details resulted from improper use of artificial intelligence in the article's creation. Reported impact The fabricated article was distributed through NTB to multiple news outlets, including Finansavisen and Nettavisen. As of the reporting date, the article remained accessible on some news websites despite NTB's retraction notification. Index analysis The AI tool generated quotations that did not exist in the source material, some appearing to be exaggerations or distortions of points in Telenor's report rather than direct paraphrasing. Governance controls NTB's editorial standards were not followed in the article's production, specifically sections 3.2 and 3.7 of their guidelines.
AII-1001-41991: A video generated using OpenAI's Sora tool depicting an armed military incursion into Spain's Congress circulated on X and TikTok with over 6 million views. The 10-second video showed soldiers pointing weapons at officials and contained audio of an arrest, accompanied by false claims that the Garde civile and Spanish army had entered Congress to arrest corrupt legislators. Fact-checking revealed the video was artificial. The original video, published on 15 October 2025 by a TikTok account describing itself as a creator of AI image content, bore Sora's watermark. Users subsequently removed or obscured the watermark before sharing the video widely, which accumulated over 254,000 views on the original post. Reported impact The synthetic video reached over 6 million views across X and TikTok and was presented as real documentation of a coup attempt, spreading false claims about military action against Spanish government officials. Index analysis Sora allows users to generate photorealistic videos with minimal effort. The tool applies a watermark to all generated content, but removal tools exist and users in this case obscured the Sora branding with emojis. The incident illustrates how synthetic video generation can blur the line between authentic and artificial content on social platforms.
AII-1001-40749: Authors Molly Tanzer and Jennifer Gilmore filed a proposed class action lawsuit against Salesforce on Wednesday, alleging the company used thousands of copyrighted books without permission to train its xGen AI models. The complaint stated that Salesforce infringed copyrights by using the authors' work and that of others to train xGen to process language. Reported impact The lawsuit alleges that content creators were not fairly compensated for their work used in AI training. Index analysis Attorney Joseph Saveri, representing the authors, stated that companies using copyrighted material for AI products should be transparent and fairly compensate content creators. Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff has previously criticized AI companies for using 'stolen' training data and stated that paying content creators would be 'very easy to do,' according to the complaint. Governance controls Salesforce declined to comment on the lawsuit.
AII-1001-40709: Actor Akshay Kumar filed a John Doe suit before the Bombay High Court seeking protection of his personality rights from unknown persons infringing them via artificial intelligence. He seeks to restrain unknown persons from unauthorised commercial exploitation of his name, screen name, image, likeness, voice, distinctive performance style, mannerisms, and other identifiable attributes through AI-generated and deepfake images and videos, counterfeit merchandise, deceptive advertisements, false brand endorsements, and impersonating social media profiles. Reported impact Kumar's personality rights, publicity rights, celebrity rights, right to privacy, and right to live with dignity under Article 21 of the Constitution of India have been infringed through large-scale misuse of his persona across social media platforms and e-commerce sites. Index analysis Kumar is seeking protection of his moral rights under the Copyright Act, 1957. The suit names social media platforms and e-commerce sites as parties to the case, with a hearing scheduled before the Bombay High Court. Governance controls Justice Arif Doctor recently granted interim protection of similar personality rights to playback singer Asha Bhosle and actor Suniel Shetty, with the High Court recognising that unauthorised creation and uploading of deepfake images on social media platforms constitutes infringement of personality rights.
AII-1001-40653: Commonwealth Bank made 45 workers redundant earlier in 2025 after unknowingly training an AI chatbot that executives intended to replace them. Kathryn Sullivan spent years helping to train the AI chatbot without being aware that the technology would be used to eliminate her position. Reported impact Kathryn Sullivan described the experience as devastating after losing her job at the bank. Staff had to be re-engaged following the redundancies, a process CEO Matt Comyn described as 'unnecessarily challenging'. Index analysis The bank's handling of the AI implementation failed to adequately consider business and employee relations implications. CBA acknowledged that future adoption of emerging technology needed to be done respectfully and with appropriate employee engagement. Governance controls At the bank's annual general meeting on 15 October 2025, chairman Paul O'Malley admitted 'We made a mistake. We didn't adequately consider all the relevant business considerations.' O'Malley stated the bank would need to 'do that respectfully' in future and ensure proper support if employees are impacted. CEO Comyn said it was 'incumbent upon us to engage appropriately and determine whether any roles will be impacted'.
AII-1001-40629: Italian newspaper publishers associated with Fieg filed a formal complaint with Agcom, Italy's communications regulator, on 15 October 2025 against Google's AI Overviews service. According to the complaint, Google integrates AI-generated responses directly into search results, which discourages users from clicking through to original publisher websites. The complaint highlights that the AI Mode function—a button in Google Search that places AI responses in the center of the page and relegates links to a sidebar—exacerbates the problem. European publishers in Enpa have also raised the issue with digital services coordinators in other EU countries, seeking an investigation by the European Commission under the Digital Services Act. Reported impact Publishers claim AI Overviews and AI Mode reduce the visibility and accessibility of their content, causing them to lose advertising revenue. The Fieg complaint states that the economic sustainability of news websites is threatened by this competition with AI-generated summaries. Index analysis Fieg argues in its technical note that Google violates fundamental Digital Services Act provisions with effects prejudicial to Italian users, consumers, and businesses. The complaint characterizes Google as a 'traffic killer' that diverts users from original news sources and threatens the sustainability of quality journalism and plurality of information.
AII-1001-40563: About 190 students at Yonsei University were caught cheating on a midterm exam for a course on natural language processing and ChatGPT using unauthorized methods. The course had about 600 students enrolled, was conducted entirely online, and the exam was administered remotely through a designated website with multiple-choice questions. A poll of 353 online community respondents showed roughly 190 admitted to using unauthorized methods while 163 said they completed the exam on their own. At Seoul National University, some students used AI tools to solve problems during a midterm exam for a statistics course, despite the school's explicit warning not to use AI during the test. The exam was conducted in person using computers in a classroom. At Korea University, about 500 students were caught exchanging answers in a group chat online during a midterm exam for a massive open online class with over 1,400 students. The test was conducted entirely online without proctoring tools such as camera monitoring or remote exam security software. Reported impact Students and campus observers expressed frustration over the large-scale cheating incidents, saying those who broke the rules should be held accountable. However, observers noted that given the anonymous nature of over 10 open chat rooms related to Korea University's course, it will be nearly impossible to identify every student who took part. Index analysis The incidents highlight vulnerabilities in remote and online exam administration across universities. At Korea University, the course lacked proctoring tools, and at Seoul National University, students had access to AI tools despite warnings and in-person supervision. Yonsei University had AI use guidelines in place since last year and updated them in September, but the university acknowledged that the guidelines function more as recommended practices than enforceable rules. The large-scale nature of online courses with thousands of students, which expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, poses challenges for ensuring academic integrity. Governance controls Korea University voided the midterm exam and plans to increase the final exam from 35 to about 100 questions with strict time limits, randomize question order in real time, and activate 'Trust Lock' software to block screen sharing and recording. The university is conducting random live monitoring and investigating how many students were involved, though it has not yet decided whether to adopt these measures campus-wide. Yonsei University's professor vowed to take strict action, offering students who come forward voluntarily a zero on the midterm but no further penalties, while those who do not could face suspension in line with university regulations. Seoul National University is reportedly considering nullifying the midterm results and holding a retest.
AII-1001-40541: AI search results have generated inaccurate information about hunting and fishing regulations in Wyoming and Idaho. Wyoming Game and Fish reported that AI-generated search results referenced failed legislative bills as if they were current law, in some cases providing information in direct opposition to actual laws and regulations. Idaho Fish and Game Conservation Officers encountered people in the field using AI and search engines to obtain season dates and regulations, resulting in citations for violations. Reported impact Wyoming Game and Fish warned that individuals relying on inaccurate AI-generated interpretations of wildlife laws could face hunting or fishing violations, with potential consequences including fines, jail time, or suspension of hunting and fishing privileges. Index analysis Search engines including Google include disclaimers that AI-generated information may not be accurate, placing responsibility on individuals to verify responses through official sources. Governance controls Wyoming and Idaho Game and Fish departments directed the public to official agency websites, printed regulations, and direct contact with offices rather than relying on AI-generated search results.
AII-1001-42129: On October 14, 2025, the Delhi High Court directed Google to use its technology to stop fake advertisements on YouTube featuring AI-generated images and deepfake videos of Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev. Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora ordered Google to immediately halt ads depicting Sadhguru's arrest and asked Google and Isha Foundation representatives to meet and work out a lasting solution. The court noted that Google's own policies prohibit clickbait ads surrounding negative life events like arrests or deaths, and that under India's intermediary rules, the platform is required to proactively identify and block previously removed infringing content. Reported impact Despite a May 2025 Delhi High Court ruling that granted protection to Sadhguru's personality rights and directed Google to suspend or take down fake and misleading content, deceptive ads have reportedly continued to appear on YouTube, misleading viewers and enabling online scams. In an earlier case, a 57-year-old retired woman in Bengaluru lost Rs 3.75 crore to scammers who used an AI-generated deepfake video of Sadhguru to promote fake investment opportunities. Index analysis The court pointed out that Google had failed to comply with its own policies and India's intermediary guidelines despite a prior ruling in May 2025. Google's counsel stated it was willing to take a collaborative approach and would actively cooperate in taking down any further links pointed out to them. Governance controls The court directed Google to either remove the content immediately or file an affidavit detailing any technological limitations or reservations preventing compliance with the order.
AII-1001-40437: A 33-year-old woman who had fled to Poland during Russia's full-scale invasion organized a criminal group that obtained personal data of online banking users from unidentified sources, including financial account numbers, mobile phone numbers, passwords, and authorization codes. The group conducted unauthorized access to Ukrainian bank mobile applications and the Diia government app through BankID authentication systems. After gaining access to citizens' electronic cabinets, they downloaded digital documents and the organizer created short deepfake videos by overlaying victims' faces onto her own face to bypass automated photo-verification in banking systems. Using this method, the group opened accounts and contracts in the names of at least 286 Ukrainian citizens and obtained loans exceeding 4 million hryvnia for some of them. The stolen funds were transferred to controlled accounts across various financial institutions, then converted to cryptocurrency and cashed out. Reported impact At least 286 Ukrainian citizens had accounts opened in their names without authorization, with loans exceeding 4 million hryvnia issued fraudulently. Index analysis The use of deepfake technology to create fake identity verification videos represents a novel application of AI for financial fraud, exploiting the reliance of automated banking systems on biometric verification. Governance controls The National Police of Ukraine investigation revealed that financial institutions' automated photo-verification systems were vulnerable to deepfake manipulation, lacking adequate safeguards against synthetic media.
